newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Heavy wins order for generators in Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Heavy wins order for generators in Taiwan.

text.p: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd said on Wednesday that it had won an order to supply generators for a nuclear power plant in Taiwan.
The order was worth an estimated $120 million, a company spokesman said.
The generators will be installed in nuclear reactors to be built by Japanese electric machinery makers Hitachi Ltd and Toshiba Corp, the spokesman said.
The reactors will be built in Japan and shipped to Taiwan in three to four years, a Hitachi spokesman said.
They are for Taiwan Power Co's fourth nuclear power plant to be constructed east of Taipei.
Funding for the controversial project was restored by Taiwan's parliament earlier this month after being cut in May after strong protests by local residents.
The Hitachi spokesman said Japanese electric machinery makers hope to capitalise on the growing demand for nuclear power plant components in Asia.
By the end of 1995 there were 28 nuclear power plant projects in Asia outside of Japan, according to the Japan Atomic Industrial Forum, a government-affiliated institution.
